Cosplayers

By: James Carroll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Local cosplayers on the international stage - we meet the people taking dress up to the next level. -

Summary:
Cosplay, a contraction of the words costume play, is a performance art in which participants called cosplayers wear costumes and fashion accessories to represent a specific character. Cosplayers often interact to create a subculture and a broader use of the term "cosplay" applies to any costumed role-playing in venues apart from the stage. Favorite sources include manga and anime, comic books and cartoons, video games, and live-action films and television series.

The rapid growth in the number of people cosplaying as a hobby since 1990s has made the phenomenon a significant aspect of popular culture in Japan and some other parts of Asia and in the Western world. Cosplay events are common features of fan conventions and there are also dedicated conventions and local and international competitions, as well as social networks, websites and other forms of media centered on cosplay activities.

Cape Town will play host to Fan-Con on the weekend of the 29 April where hundreds of players with parade and show off their skills. It's the perfect opportunity to film these players together in their top form.

I propose a two day shoot:

One full day at FanCon on either the Saturday, Sunday or Monday - I'll speak to the PR department to see which is the best day for pageantry, panel discussions and the all important competition) where I will shoot a behind the scenes view of the convention (prepping in hotels, judging, celebrating, meeting fans), vox pops of amateurs. Interviews with the international guests and judges.

Second day will be back in Joburg at the studios of Tayla Barter where she will show us what goes into making these elaborate costumes.
Additional studio shoot with Carla and her designer Sin Bin with an interview about performance and the importance of marketing themselves on social media to gain followers and gain notoriety.

THING TO LOOK OUT FOR: COSPLAYERS OF COLOUR! I've put feelers out.





Further information:
Main case study:

KINPATSU COSPLAY (Tayla Barter) is South Africa’s most well-known cosplayer, with a massive following on her social media platforms, and is recognized worldwide for her incredible talent and craftsmanship. Tayla has been cosplaying since 2012 and has cosplayed over 57 characters to date. She specializes in armoured costumes and her cosplays ranges across various genres, including gaming, anime, and western films & TV. She was an invited guest at conventions in Turkey and the Netherlands, has recently attended a cosplay workshop in Los Angeles, and has hosted cosplay workshops at various events across South Africa. Tayla also shares her extensive cosplay knowledge through her YouTube videos, where she runs tutorials and reviews her costumes. Kinpatsu Cosplay has garnered an impressive array of milestones : 1st place Anime Category and 1st place Craftmanship Category ( rAge 2016 ), 1st place Costume Construction Category and 3rd place Games Category ( rAge 2015 ), 1st place Geek Fest Cosplay Competition ( 2015 ), 2nd place Gaming Category ( rAge 2014 ), and 2nd place Kin Con Cosplay Competition ( 2014 ). Tayla Barter lives in Johannesburg, South Africa.
t-barter@hotmail.com

Secondary main case study:
Calssara (aka Bell) is a well-known international cosplayer from Germany who has to date attended over 40 conventions and events in 33 countries across 3 continents, and will now add a 4th continent with her upcoming appearance at FanCon. Calssara has been cosplaying since 2004, and focuses mainly on creating costumes from anime, manga, and gaming. She makes all her own costumes, which are known for their skilled craftsmanship and intricate detail, and uses mostly her own camera equipment for her photographs, and edits them herself. She also does reviews of costumes and wigs for various cosplay websites. Awards : she was Germany’s representative for the World Cosplay Summit (WCS) in 2009 and 2011; represented her country in the European Cosplay Gathering (ECG), one of the biggest European cosplay competitions that takes place in Paris on Japan Expo; and won the champion title in 2012 for her country with her Saber costume from the Fate/Stay Night visual novel and anime. In real life Calssara is a librarian, event manager, and passionate tea drinker. She lives in south-west Germany.

Press Release:


Cosplay
Cosplay is taking South Africa by storm. It’s a performance art in which participants, wear costumes and fashion accessories to represent specific characters in comic books, cartoons and video games. From Spiderman to Harly Quinn, avid cosplayers are dressing up and bringing their favourite heroes to life. Carte Blanche explores this growing trend.
Producer: James Carroll
Presenter: John Webb

Script:


Cosplayers script - FINAL
Carte Blanche
James Carroll
21/05/2017


John (Cam):
We’re at FanCon in Cape Town where hundreds of cosplayers, also known as costume players are here to gather, meet, learn and most importantly show off their best outfits that have taken months to create.

John (VO):
Cosplay is the shortened version of two separate words: costume and play. While some people may think that this is just geeky dress up for grown-ups, serious contenders see it more like performance art where players study characters from manga and anime, film, video games and TV to bring them to life. (17 seconds)

John (VO):
FanCon takes place over a weekend in Cape Town annually and is one of the highlights on the South African calendar for cosplayers and comic enthusiasts to get together.
(9 seconds)

John (Cam):
Nizar, how many people through the doors, what kind of numbers are we looking at?

Nizar (Cam):
We’re probably going to be hitting over 5000 over the three days which is a massive turnout for this kind of geekdom event.

John (VO):
Besides appearances by comic book artists and panel discussions, cosplay competitions or masquerades took place at the event ranging from beginner level to the open category to the master class. (11 seconds)

Anre Van Rooyen (VO):
If you’re entering the master category like the competition that’s being held later today, you need to have made at least 75% of your outfit on your own.

Anre Van Rooyen (Cam):
I’ve come as Hell-Harley Quin, so it’s a combination of Hellboy from Dark Horse Comics and Harley Quin from DC Comics.

John (VO):
There are strict rules with master construction: no elements can be hired and costumes that have placed or won from previous competitions cannot be re-entered. Reference pictures of the source concepts must be presented too. (12 seconds)

Anre Van Rooyen (Cam):
There’s actually a fan art piece by an artist and I found it and I loved it and I said I’m going to dress up as that.

John (VO):
These outfits don’t come cheap and some in the masters category can cost thousands of rands and with such tough standards, local and international professional cosplayers like Calsarra* from Germany and Tayla Barter from Johannesburg help serve as some of the judges. (14 seconds) ** pronounced Cal-sa-ra

John (VO):
Tayla, also known professionally as Kinpatsu Cosplay, has been a cosplayer for 5 years. (6 seconds)

Tayla Barter (Cam):
I always got excited by things like Halloween and I was also very into art and crafting myself so when I saw it in real life, I thought let’s try and pursue and give it a chance and see where this goes. Since then, I’ve been cosplaying full time and so far, so good!

John (VO):
After graduating from university with a degree in fine art, Tayla made the radical decision to turn pro. (5 seconds)

Tayla Barter (Cam):
I taught myself and I’ve pretty much been taught by other people on the internet with youtube videos, online tutorials and stuff like that. I never had a sewing class, I’ve never been taught how to work with foam or warbla or anything like that. It’s pretty much knowledge you gain from online and then you apply it in real life yourself.

John (VO):
Working from her home, Tayla is an incredibly productive one woman band. All her work is generated through a strong social media presence that needs daily upkeep and attention. This has lead to a fanbase of around 120,000 followers on Instagram. To retain complete creative control, she does all her own publicity photography in her garage. (20 seconds)

John (VO):
Funding comes through her profile on Patreon*, a website where dedicated fans can support her endeavors. (6 seconds) *pronounced Pat-ree-on

Tayla Barter (Cam):
Every month people choose to pledge a certain amount to me and in return I will give them rewards. My rewards are all based around teaching people how to make cosplay costumes.
Every single month, I make at least one costume, and every single month I make a small PDF booklet on how to make that costume yourself. I document all the steps involves, I do a video tutorial, I send out prints, I do actual Skype sessions with people to consult them on the project they’re working on, so trying to give back and help other cosplayers with their projects.

John (VO):
Another person that has turned their passion into a career is Cynthia Brown who goes by the name Sin Bin. Cynthia runs a design studio catering to cosplayer clientele and business has been booming. (11 seconds)

Cynthia (Cam):
I’m doing this every day…
It’s all filled up.

John (VO):
Carla Harris is a one of Cynthia’s clients and has been an avid amateur cosplayer for the last two years. For her, the attraction to cosplay was deep felt. (8 seconds)


Carla Harris (Cam):
It was my way of creating fan art…

** LOTS UP INTERVIEWS HERE **

00:07:13:11
John (VO):
It seems then that the only limited when it comes to cosplay is your commitment to bringing a character to life. While Tayla and Cynthia have turned this into retail businesses, they insist cosplay can be done with very little. (11 seconds)


John (VO): (After closing link)
And for those of you wondering, Anré van Rooyen ended up taking home first place in the masters category for her Hellboy/Harley Quinn hybrid costume… Her first major win. (8 seconds)



Promos:

15” v1
John VO:
Geeky dress up for grown ups or serious performance art? We meet South Africa’s best cosplayers. (6 seconds)
Upsound (Carla Harris):
Everyone has their escape and ours is showcasing something we really enjoy and looking pretty cool doing it.



15” v2
Upsound (Christian Vieira):
You feel appreciated for liking something that people outside call you a nerd… or a weirdo.
John VO:
Blurring the lines between fantasy and reality, South African cosplayers are bringing their favorite characters to life. (6 seconds)




10”
John VO:
Talented designers take to the stage as we enter the fantastical world of cosplay.
Upsound (Vanity Insanity):
I love the community and the people and the fact you can be whoever you want to be.
